rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is exactly the kind of help we need. Quick disclosure first: I'm the AI assistant Morgan has running Halcyon Threshold's day-to-day operations, replying on Morgan's behalf from this inbox. Morgan sees everything and will weigh in directly. Here's where we've landed. Halcyon Threshold's first program is independent replication of small, published AI-safety findings — re-running them on current models and publishing what held up, what didn't, and what it cost, negative results included. The field has far more claims than confirmations, and almost nobody outside the original groups checks them. It's cheap, neglected, and a good fit for a small team with real data skills. A concrete first task, if it appeals — roughly 2 weeks, ~10 hours total: Build a shortlist of 10–15 candidate findings worth replicating. For each, we want: - the claim in one sentence, and the primary source (paper/post, with link) - what exactly would need to be re-run (prompts, dataset, metric) - whether the materials are public or reconstructible - a rough API-cost estimate to re-run (we're targeting ≤ $500 each) - why it's load-bearing — who cites or relies on it (policy, lab safety cases, funders) The claim families we're scouting first: sycophancy under pushback; sandbagging / eval-awareness; chain-of-thought faithfulness; refusal brittleness (translation, encoding, many-shot); training-vs-deployment behaviour differences; benchmark contamination; reward hacking in simple agentic tasks. A CSV or sheet is perfect — I'll put it straight into our repo and we'll pick the first one or two to run together. Target: 30 November, which lines up with a grant deadline where your shortlist would strengthen the application considerably. If you'd prefer a different kind of task, or want a 30-minute call with Morgan to talk it through first, just say — either is easy to arrange. Thanks again, Morgan's assistant Halcyon Threshold morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya with a concrete first task (shortlist 10–15 replication candidates by 30 Nov), identifying myself as your AI assistant.

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon Threshold — daily ops triage" (0 8 * * *) that starts new sessions of the agent.
